construction.name: complete_axial_slot_column_return
construction.proof:
COMPLETE AXIAL-SLOT COLUMN WEAVE, PR5 N96

The source is the reviewed common-axis subdivision of the complete
48-parent height-two published double-lattice return. Its 16 planar
(lattice i,lattice j,motif) labels each occur at all three original axial
levels. After subdivision there are two height-one children per parent.
For each planar source label and each child slot, take its three complete
children as one rigid block. This yields 32 actual column blocks, all96
owners, and preserves every source quaternion and finite displacement.

The proposed operation gives each column block one common translation,
with a single shared cube side. It releases the former requirement that
both axial-slot copies of each parent column follow the same displacement.
Within-block geometry remains unchanged; every cross-block pair retains
one complete actual separating row from the native source. Every vertex
must satisfy all six actual cube walls. All block variables and the host
side are solved together, with one common restoration back toward the
known source. No independent pair placement, frame change or angle sweep
is permitted. A realized path must keep a common separator for every pair
at both rounded endpoints, including pairs within the rigid columns.

The starting source, full parent/slot inverse map and every column label
remain controls. A negative linear result is only for the selected native
contact map; an equal-value return remains a distinct geometry if it
changes the column interface. This is a full-child composition operation,
not the individual H<h collar inclusion studied in the other lane.

construction.name: common_axis_affine_then_full_axial_subdivision
construction.proof:
COMMON-AXIS AFFINE TRANSFER FOLLOWED BY COMPLETE AXIAL SUBDIVISION

Inherited controls are common_axis_prism_transfer/SOURCE_DECODER.txt and
review/constructive/AXIAL_SUBDIVISION_LEMMA.txt. Earlier public axial work
permits kH=h (and triangle/hexagon base subdivisions with uniform scaling).
It does not include this general axial-only common stretch kH/h while
leaving the canonical base unchanged. Those earlier identities remain
controls and their reviewed cases are included in comparison gates.

For a complete source of n regular prisms P_h with actual common axis
R_i e3=epsilon_i d, let k be an integer >=2 with kn<=100. For target height
H in {1,3/2,2,3}, put r=kH/h and A=I+(r-1)dd^T/(d.d). Apply A to every
complete source owner and center simultaneously. Its owner i is now
Ac_i+R_i P_(kH). A is invertible, so distinct full parents stay disjoint.

For each complete parent i introduce ALL slots j=0,...,k-1 with centers
  Ac_i + R_i ((j-(k-1)/2) H e3),
and the same actual frame R_i. Their closed axial intervals partition
[-kH/2,kH/2] and their common base is exactly the source/target canonical
polygon. They are complete height-H owners. The sign epsilon_i is not
ignored: offsets use the actual frame R_i. All sibling pairs have the
parent axial separator and all cross-parent pairs inherit one transformed
source separator A^{-T}u. No independent choice of pair translation occurs.

Compute the full transformed parent union's coordinate bounds from every
actual canonical source vertex under A. That is exactly the full child
union; no axial end cost is dropped. Recenter their common box once, then
apply one common center dilation rho>1 and outward cube restoration as in
the reviewed subdivision lemma. Native centers and unchanged quaternions
are checked on every actual wall and every sibling/cross-parent pair.

The inverse retains source path/hash/Git provenance and authors, n,k,h,H,
rational d,A,A^{-1}, common box midpoint and rho, and the complete ordered
(parent index i, slot j) map. Subtract the inherited axial slot offset and
invert A to recover the original parent center. No proper subset or count
is promoted in the present screen. The bounded k range follows kn<=100,
not a coordinate or angle search. The r=1 cases preserve earlier controls.

construction.name: two_owner_pentagonal_double_lattice_return

source_control.proof:
PENTAGON DOUBLE-LATTICE MARKED RETURN
15 October 2026

Source reading: Kallus and Kusner, arXiv:1509.02241, sections 2.2, 2.3, 3.1,
https://arxiv.org/html/1509.02241 . The infinite construction is attributed
to Greg Kuperberg and Wlodzimierz Kuperberg (1990); the explicit coordinates
are reconstructed from Kallus and Kusner. No source optimality is claimed as
new, and no plane-optimality assertion is needed for the finite witnesses.

Use native unit-edge pentagon vertices k0,...,k4 counterclockwise from the
positive x axis. Let p1=k0, p4=(k2+k3)/2, p2=(k0+3k1)/4, p6=(3k4+k0)/4.
The two return generators are b0=p1-p4 and b1=2(p2-p6). The latter is the
composition of two actual point reflections through p2,p6; the former is
twice a chord of the inscribed half-length parallelogram. A source word
(i,j,t) realizes B(i,j)+m_t+R_t K, where m0=0,m1=2p2 and R0=I,R1=-I.

The exact canonical quartic field verifies every one of the 34 nontrivial
ordered motif/short-word comparisons, using support of R_a K-R_b K rather
than an assumed central symmetry. For every omitted word some |zi|>=2;
the corresponding center coordinate exceeds 2R because 2Bii-mi>2R and every
base vertex has coordinate absolute value at most R. This is a complete
periodic proof, not an empirical neighborhood check. Source_control retains
all axes, supports, short words, tail slacks, and the four marked points.

Extrude over the full height [-L/2,L/2] and add period (0,0,L). Equal vertical
indices inherit the proved planar separator; different indices separate on
z. The second frame is the proper spatial halfturn diag(-1,-1,1), with the
exact native quaternion (0,0,0,1). Thus no owner is reflected improperly.

Finite operation: cut complete owners around an actual source boundary mark,
including p2,p6 with their native vertex indices and barycentric weights.
For each target count preserve the full source word, motif label, initial
center and host scale. At every continuation step select a separator that
already separates the preceding whole-owner pair; restore all host walls
simultaneously in one common linear system. Keep the resulting full centers,
all pair indices, every predecessor and fixed motif frame. A failed solver
is retained as a complete predecessor, not treated as an obstruction.

The published source receives a common 1.000001 dilation before numerical
realization. Native witnesses scale final centers by 1.0000001 and use the
same host factor plus 1e-7. Every native whole-owner pair and host wall is
then checked by the official exact-input verifier. Finite gains are compared
against both the full pinned public tree including community files and the
strongest retained own witness. Source density alone does not establish a
finite gain; all counts pay their actual boundary costs.

contribution.method:
This is an explicit replacement archive for 23 previously submitted cases, adding zero new distinct campaign cases. SUPERSESSIONS.json identifies the prior issue, archive, native hash and certified scale for each case. Ten replacements improve the pinned current nominal/reference bound; thirteen improve the complete native certificate without claiming a new ideal nominal value.

These complete constructions combine forced-phase prism-to-antiprism ring/slot inclusion, literal whole-owner prefixes, prism column and height/collar transfers, and retained whole-row returns. Every source has a full physical decoder with actual owner centers and frames. Certificate improvements arise from these physical operations; their narrower numerical scope is retained explicitly.

All active witnesses passed independent source, full geometry and current-public/private comparison review, followed by both official checks on the packaged native files. The archive preserves the complete source chain, original donor attribution, reviewed intermediate packings and explicit supersession identities. Some provenance audit scripts require the authenticated upstream Git snapshot or reviewed-source registry; the bundled official native validators are directly replayable.

Credit the new finite constructions exactly to PingYou Ltd. Original donors and their authors remain credited. These contributions may be published under the repository’s MIT license. No global optimum is claimed. Please treat these as stronger replacements, not as 23 additional distinct cases.
